subject.title: fix(doctor): bound legacy sessions.json reads during SQLite inspect

question: Should doctor continue to migrate valid legacy `sessions.json` files above 16 MiB, or is rejecting them with operator-led cleanup an approved persistent-session support boundary?
rationale: The implementation is mechanically coherent, but it intentionally changes what existing persistent user data doctor will migrate; code and tests cannot determine whether that product and upgrade trade-off is acceptable.

options.title: Preserve oversized-store migration
options.body: Require a bounded migration approach that can process valid legacy stores above 16 MiB without allocating the entire file at once.

options.title: Approve the 16 MiB boundary
options.body: Accept the fail-closed limit as the supported migration contract and confirm that backup plus non-destructive reduction guidance is sufficient for affected users.

options.title: Pause for owner decision
options.body: Do not merge until the doctor/session SQLite owner selects one of the supported upgrade contracts.

recommendation.title: Pause for owner decision
recommendation.body: Do not merge until the doctor/session SQLite owner selects one of the supported upgrade contracts.

likelyOwner.reason: The available context does not provide reliable feature-history attribution, so the decision should be routed to the identified doctor/session SQLite code owner.
